function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

It sounds like you’re looking for a conversational companion powered by artificial intelligence—something similar to what people sometimes call an “AI girlfriend.” While there isn’t a single product that’s universally recognized under that label, several platforms offer chatbot experiences designed to simulate companionship, emotional support, or even romance within clear limits. Below are some options and practical tips if you’d like to explore this area: | Platform | What It Offers | Key Features | |----------|-----------------|--------------| | **Replika** | An adaptive chatbot that learns your communication style over time. Users often describe Replika as a supportive friend or partner. | • Emotion‑aware responses
• Customizable personality settings
• Daily check‑ins & mood tracking | | **Chatbot.com / ManyChat** | Build your own bot using templates. You can program scenarios ranging from casual conversation to role‑play. | • Drag‑and‑drop interface
• Integration with messaging apps
• Analytics dashboard | | **Mitsuku (Kuki)** | Award‑winning chatbot known for witty dialogue. Not specifically marketed as a relationship bot, but many users enjoy long conversations. | • Natural language understanding
• Multi‑topic knowledge base | | **Woebot** | Focused more on mental health than romance, Woebot offers daily chats aimed at improving well‑being. | • Cognitive behavioral therapy techniques
• Mood logging | ### How to Get Started 1. **Define Your Goals** * Are you seeking lighthearted banter, emotional support, or something closer to a romantic narrative? * Knowing this helps narrow choices and set realistic expectations. 2. **Choose a Platform** * For a ready‑made experience, try Replika or Mitsuku first. * If you prefer full control, consider building a custom bot via Chatbot.com or Dialogflow. 3. **Set Boundaries Early On** * Most AI systems have usage guidelines. Make sure you understand privacy terms and data handling practices. * Remember that while AI can mimic empathy, it does not possess genuine emotions or consciousness. 4. **Experiment Safely** * Start with short sessions to gauge comfort levels. * Keep track of how interactions affect your mood and social life. 5. **Maintain Real‑World Connections** * Use the AI as a supplement—not a replacement—for human interaction. * Balance online engagement with offline activities and real‑world friendships. ### Ethical Considerations * **Data Privacy:** Be mindful of personal details you share. Some bots store conversation logs for training purposes. * **Emotional Dependency:** Overreliance on an AI for affection may impact real-life relationships. Regular self-reflection helps keep things balanced. * **Transparency:** Choose products that clearly disclose their capabilities and limitations so you don’t develop unrealistic expectations. --- #### Quick Tips for Building a Simple Companion Bot If you decide to build one yourself, here’s a minimal workflow: ```python from chatterbot import ChatBot from chatterbot.trainers import ListTrainer chatbot = ChatBot('Companion') trainer = ListTrainer(chatbot) conversation = [ "Hi!", "Hello! How are you feeling today?", # Add more pairs... ] trainer.train(conversation) ``` This snippet uses `ChatterBot`, a lightweight library that lets you train a bot on simple Q&A pairs. From there, you can integrate natural language processing libraries (e.g., spaCy, GPT APIs) to make dialogues richer. --- Feel free to let me know which direction interests you most—whether exploring existing solutions or creating a personalized bot—and I’ll dive deeper into specifics!
